artwork.title: I Beat The World’s Best Video Game
artwork.alt: One real-life Stokes twin stands waist-up at the LEFT, looking at camera in amazed pride, both hands presenting an enormous floating Minecraft-built Earth on the RIGHT. The sphere is a clearly readable single object: its near hemisphere has bright blocky Minecraft grass and mountains; one curved quadrant is a modern GTA city with recognizable roads and a red supercar; a purple portal seam between the two worlds spills a tiny formation of Halo Flood and Call of Duty zombies onto the grass. A small black block-built Ender Dragon circles the sphere. Make the real human the creator of this impossible world, not a game avatar.

artwork.title: I Beat The World’s Best Video Game
artwork.alt: One real-life Stokes twin crouches in the LEFT foreground of a bright Minecraft meadow, turning toward camera in shocked excitement, one hand pulling the edge of an enormous upright obsidian portal. The violet portal fills the RIGHT half of frame. Through it is a sunlit modern GTA city, and a red realistic supercar is bursting OUT over the threshold toward the viewer, its nose and front tires outside the portal. Behind the car inside the portal are a small legible cluster of three invading enemies: one Halo Flood combat form with a distorted asymmetrical silhouette and tentacle arm, one ragged Call of Duty zombie, and one green Minecraft creeper. The car casts a contact shadow on the Minecraft grass. This is clearly two game worlds meeting through one physical doorway.

artwork.title: I Beat The World’s Best Video Game
artwork.alt: One real-life Stokes twin rides astride the neck of the black block-built Minecraft Ender Dragon as it flies directly TOWARD the camera. The host is close and photographic, with a huge open-mouthed excited expression, windswept hair, wearing a simple black T-shirt. He holds a realistic black machine gun securely across his body, muzzle angled down and away from the viewer. The dragon has a blocky square head, unmistakable purple eyes and broad angular wings extending to both sides. Behind them, a single violet portal in a Minecraft cliff has released a looming Halo Flood combat form, two Call of Duty zombies and a creeper; they chase across a block bridge below. Clearly an escape toward the viewer, with the threat behind the rider.

artwork.title: I Beat The World’s Best Video Game
artwork.alt: One real-life Stokes twin riding the black Minecraft Ender Dragon occupies the LEFT foreground, in profile facing RIGHT while his face turns enough toward camera to be recognizable. He grips a realistic machine gun with both hands, aiming toward one gigantic Halo Flood combat form on the RIGHT. The giant Flood is a recognizable infected humanoid with a hulking asymmetrical body and long tentacled arm, exaggerated but non-gory, rising behind a Minecraft hillside. Its silhouette looms much larger than the rider. One tiny creeper and one ragged Call of Duty zombie at its feet establish the ridiculous scale. The host has fierce surprised determination. The dragon square head and purple eyes are visible.

artwork.title: I Beat The World’s Best Video Game
artwork.alt: One real-life Stokes twin is large in the CENTER foreground, bracing with both arms out in astonishment as two enormous floating game-world islands collide behind him. The LEFT island is a sunny modern GTA city with clean roads, skyscrapers and a single vivid red supercar skidding toward the edge. The RIGHT island is a lush block-built Minecraft landscape, with an obsidian violet portal on a hill and a black Ender Dragon banking above it. The two islands meet at ONE dramatic glowing purple seam in the middle distance; block fragments and road pieces fly upward along that seam. At the seam a small cluster of Halo Flood combat forms, Call of Duty zombies and creepers is crossing from one world into the other. Make it a coherent physical collision, not panels or tiny franchise windows.

artwork.title: I Beat The World’s Best Video Game
artwork.alt: A real-life Stokes host fills the LEFT foreground, hanging safely from a helicopter hoist harness and looking at camera in shocked excitement. At RIGHT, an enormous cyan pixel-cut Minecraft diamond, larger than a house, hangs on a thick cable beneath a recognizable GTA Cargobob cargo helicopter. Below the diamond is a small block-built Minecraft bank with an orange oval Portal exit opening in its roof; the diamond has just been pulled through. One coherent sunny Minecraft landscape with a distant realistic GTA skyline. The huge diamond is the single hero object, with helicopter small enough to establish its scale. No police swarm or extra creatures.

artwork.title: I Beat The World’s Best Video Game
artwork.alt: A real-life Stokes host is large at LEFT, visible waist-up through the open driver's side of a glossy red GTA supercar, face turned toward camera with ecstatic shock. The car launches diagonally from lower-left toward upper-right across one missing section of Mario Kart Rainbow Road, suspended high in a luminous blue sky. A clear orange Rocket League boost plume trails from the car. One oversized blue spiny shell chases at RIGHT behind the car, visibly separated from it. Rainbow track curves once into the distance. The host, one red car and one blue shell are the only foreground groups. No other racers or HUD.

artwork.title: I Beat The World’s Best Video Game
artwork.alt: A real-life Stokes host is large at LEFT foreground, chest-up on the roof edge of one compact fortress, bracing with an amazed determined expression. The fortress fills RIGHT and has a single clean architectural cutaway: unmistakable Minecraft grass and cobblestone base, Fortnite wood ramps and metal upper walls, and a bright blue protected power core visible in its center. A small, coherent wave of ragged Call of Duty zombies approaches its base from lower-right, non-gory and secondary. One damaged wall makes the threat readable. Bright green plain and open blue sky. The fortress is one coherent building, not a collage of tiny game screenshots.

artwork.title: I Beat The World’s Best Video Game
artwork.alt: A real-life Stokes host fills LEFT foreground, chest-up gripping the side of a small rescue dinghy with a wide-eyed terrified but playful expression. One huge Sea of Thieves pirate ship occupies the RIGHT middle distance between sunlit flooded GTA skyscrapers. Use a clean natural ocean waterline across the lower third: beneath the cyan transparent water, one enormous pale Reaper Leviathan with red facial fins and four curved mandibles curls below the ship, much larger than it. Its mouth is non-gory. Above the water, blue sky and white clouds remain dominant. Keep the waterline physically continuous and the face unobscured. No extra boats, sharks or overlays.

artwork.title: I Beat The World’s Best Video Game
artwork.alt: A real-life Stokes host is large at LEFT foreground, waist-up, carefully holding one recognizable small yellow Pikachu at chest height with amazed delight. Pikachu has long black-tipped ears, red cheek circles and a lightning-bolt tail; it looks determined and friendly. A single branching yellow electricity arc crosses to the RIGHT, connecting a simple oversized Minecraft redstone relay to an enormous realistic GTA city skyline whose windows light up. One violet exit portal glows at the relay base, secondary. Bright blue sky, daylight, no night scene. Tiny Pikachu versus huge powered city is the main visual question. No other Pokémon, franchise logos or UI.

artwork.title: I Beat The World’s Best Video Game
artwork.alt: A real-life Stokes host fills the LEFT foreground, chest-up facing the camera and proudly holding a bright cyan Minecraft diamond power core, unaware of trouble behind him. At RIGHT middle ground, a red Among Us crewmate with a large cyan visor secretly pulls one oversized lever on the open door of a realistic GTA bank vault. The lever is visibly linked to one violet portal opening inside the vault, with a single Minecraft creeper stepping out. The host's real face and the red saboteur are the two main focal groups. Sunny blue sky is visible through the bank's broken roof. No knives, gore, words, accusation arrows or multiple tiny faces.

artwork.title: I Beat The World’s Best Video Game
artwork.alt: A real-life Stokes host fills LEFT foreground, waist-up holding a black-and-yellow pressure washer lance with bare hands, looking at camera in surprised disbelief. One red GTA supercar fills RIGHT, parked in a sunny open city plaza. A powerful clearly visible water jet sweeps across its middle: the front half is glossy realistic automotive metal and the back half is transformed into chunky, clean red Minecraft voxel blocks, physically joined as one car. A narrow moving spray boundary explains the transformation without panels. Some plaza pavement behind the block half has become Minecraft grass. Blue sky and distant soft skyscrapers. No dirt, muddy Rolls-Royce, cleaning brush, blue gloves or text.

artwork.title: I Beat The World’s Best Video Game
artwork.alt: A real-life Stokes host is large at LEFT foreground, leaning from the driver's window of a red GTA off-road car with mouth open in alarm. One enormous purple T-shaped Tetris tetromino hangs directly overhead at RIGHT, seconds from landing on the road. A simple staircase of already-landed bright colored tetrominoes forms the escape route up toward a small violet portal on a Minecraft cliff. Make the suspended T piece the one dominant threat, with only two landed pieces visible, clear spacing and readable geometric silhouettes. Luminous blue sky, sunlit block-built landscape. No numbers, grid overlay, extra enemies or logos.

artwork.title: I Beat The World’s Best Video Game
artwork.alt: A real-life Stokes host is large at LEFT foreground, waist-up in the passenger seat of an open-top red GTA getaway car, looking toward camera in comic disbelief and pointing at the driver. At RIGHT foreground, one large recognizable white Untitled Goose Game goose with orange beak and feet sits upright in the driver's seat, wings gripping the steering wheel and a bulging money sack beside it. Keep goose stylized like the game, human fully photographic, car premium realistic game rendering. One small police car follows in the far background on a sunny GTA city road. Blue sky, simple diagonal road perspective. The absurd goose driver is immediately readable. No extra passengers or text.

artwork.title: I Beat The World’s Best Video Game
artwork.alt: A real-life Stokes host fills LEFT foreground, chest-up standing on the shoulder platform of a giant humanoid robot, one hand gripping a rail and the other presenting the machine with triumphant amazement. The robot fills RIGHT as one coherent, clean silhouette: Minecraft iron-block torso and head, a glossy red GTA supercar integrated as its forearm with the car's front clearly visible, and one huge glowing blue Halo energy sword in its opposite hand. Feet stand on a small Minecraft hillside in front of a distant GTA skyline. A single small violet rift behind the machine establishes the mission. Use low-angle scale and luminous blue sky. No other giant enemies, loose floating props, logos or text.

artwork.title: I Filled GTA With Dinosaurs!
artwork.alt: A real-life Stokes host in a black T-shirt is CENTER foreground, waist-up standing through the open roof of a glossy red GTA supercar, face large with thrilled alarm. At RIGHT one enormous recognizable ARK Tyrannosaurus lowers its open non-gory jaw toward the back of the car, almost biting it. Its massive head dwarfs the human. At LEFT, far behind, one long-neck dinosaur steps over a tiny sunlit city bus. The host reaches toward camera as the car races forward on a broad GTA boulevard. Blue sky fills the upper third. One dominant dinosaur head, one real human and one car; background dinosaur very small. Bright playful adventure, no injury or gore.

artwork.title: I Gave My Friends Every Superpower!
artwork.alt: A photographic real-life Stokes host is large at RIGHT foreground in a clean red-and-blue Spider-Man suit with NO mask, real black hair and face fully visible. He grins in excited disbelief and fires a thick white web from his LEFT hand diagonally across the image. At LEFT a GTA police car hangs high above the ground, securely caught in a single huge web sling. Directly under the suspended car is a compact staircase of floating Minecraft grass blocks rising from a sunny GTA plaza, showing a second impossible ability. The visible web connects host wrist to car and explains the action. Luminous blue sky; low-angle camera and clean negative space. The host and one web-caught car are the two main visual groups. No extra superheroes or printed chest emblem.

artwork.title: We Built a Roller Coaster Across Video Games!
artwork.alt: Front-facing ride camera: a photographic real-life Stokes host occupies the CENTER of the image in the front seat of one bright yellow roller-coaster train. His face is very large, hair blown back, mouth open in joyous shock, both hands on the safety bar. A tiny blocky Roblox passenger sits in the next row, secondary. Behind the host the single red track dives dramatically from upper LEFT through a chunky Minecraft grass cliff and swings toward distant realistic GTA skyscrapers on the RIGHT. The near track falls sharply away below the front seat to communicate a huge drop. One uninterrupted physical track, not separated panels. Sunny blue sky and white clouds, vivid green terrain, simple coherent depth. No text, no multiple unrelated portals.

artwork.title: We Escaped the World’s Deadliest Obstacle Course!
artwork.alt: A photographic real-life Stokes host in a black T-shirt leaps from LEFT middle ground toward RIGHT foreground and toward the camera, face clearly visible in playful panic, one hand stretched forward. His foreshortened body is suspended above one enormous glowing Minecraft lava gap. One huge pink-and-white padded Fall Guys hammer swings past behind him at LEFT, nearly missing his shoes. At RIGHT foreground a single bright cyan Roblox plastic platform is the obvious safe landing target, with a blocky Roblox friend small in the far background. Use a close dramatic wide-angle viewpoint at platform height; real human contact perspective, bright blue sky upper half. One jump, one swinging hammer and one landing pad; non-gory game obstacle, not realistic injury.

artwork.title: We Escaped a Prison That Changes Games!
artwork.alt: The camera looks into a single sunlit Minecraft prison cell with an open front-wall cutaway. A photographic real-life Stokes host in an orange prison jumpsuit crouches at RIGHT foreground, face large looking to camera in amazed relief. Behind him on the LEFT a glowing blue oval Portal exit opens in the solid block-built cell wall; inside that one portal we clearly see a red GTA getaway supercar parked in a realistic sunny city street. The host reaches one arm through the portal toward the car. One pair of thick pixel iron bars hangs bent at the cell edge to show the old exit failed. Blue sky visible over the short roofless cell wall. One coherent prison space and one portal window, no split panels, no dozens of doors or tiny mazes.

artwork.title: I Controlled GTA With a Board Game!
artwork.alt: A photographic real-life Stokes host looms large at the TOP CENTER of the image behind a tabletop miniature GTA city, as if he is the giant game master. His face is large with delighted surprise; one hand releases an oversized ivory die with simple dark pips, no printed numerals or letters. The die is mid-air over the LEFT foreground. The miniature city roads form one simple squared board path of vivid Mario Party-style colored spaces curving through realistic tiny GTA skyscrapers. A glossy red GTA supercar is the main player token at RIGHT foreground, approaching one oversized red Monopoly-style hotel piece blocking its route. Camera near tabletop height creates strong scale and shallow perspective. Bright blue sky beyond the host, no board captions, no money text, no game logos. The face, die and tiny threatened car form one visual story.

artwork.title: I Turned GTA Into a Water Park!
artwork.alt: Ride-level action camera on a giant open turquoise water slide twisting between sunny GTA skyscrapers. A photographic real-life Stokes host sits on a bright yellow inflatable ring at RIGHT foreground, black T-shirt and shorts, face large and ecstatic as he looks back toward the camera over his shoulder. At LEFT the enormous slide curves sharply downward toward a distant beach pool, showing dramatic safe amusement-park scale. The middle portion of the continuous slide transforms into clean Minecraft glass and water blocks, then reconnects to a glossy Planet Coaster-style aqua flume; the transition is clear and physically joined. Bright blue sky, sunny skyline, clean cyan water splashing around the ring. One host, one uninterrupted huge slide and small pool below. No flood, creatures, pirate ships, printed signs or text.

artwork.title: We Became Ghost Hunters in GTA!
artwork.alt: A photographic real-life Stokes host occupies the RIGHT foreground, waist-up wearing a plain black T-shirt and a red-and-gray Luigi’s Mansion Poltergust vacuum backpack. His real face is large with laughing shock. He braces a dark vacuum nozzle with both hands and aims it to the LEFT. One enormous vivid red Pac-Man ghost with rounded dome, scalloped bottom and big white cartoon eyes is being pulled into the nozzle through one visible cyan spiraling suction stream, its lower body stretched toward the nozzle while its head stays huge. Sunny GTA city street recedes behind them, one tiny abandoned car and blue sky. A simple cause-and-effect diagonal connects ghost to nozzle to host. No night scene, gore, extra spirits, text, hats with logos or UI.

artwork.title: We Played Soccer With an Exploding Ball!
artwork.alt: A giant recognizable black Mario Bob-omb occupies the LEFT foreground like an enormous soccer ball, with two simple white oval eyes, brass wind-up key, small orange feet and one short fuse throwing bright harmless sparks. At RIGHT middle foreground a glossy red GTA supercar accelerates toward it; a photographic real-life Stokes host leans high through the open driver window, real face large with thrilled alarm, visibly driving. In the CENTER background one enormous Rocket League blue goal with hexagonal netting is directly behind the bomb, establishing the scoring target. Low wide camera on vibrant green pitch, luminous blue sky and simple stadium rim. The bomb is larger than the car; fuse prominent, no explosion yet, no injuries, no text or score UI.

artwork.title: I Became Faster Than Every Car in GTA!
artwork.alt: A photographic real-life Stokes host runs straight toward the camera in the CENTER foreground, waist-up and one giant foreshortened leg visible, real face large with ecstatic competitive surprise. He wears a plain black T-shirt, dark shorts and recognizable Sonic bright red running shoes with one white strap each, no character mask or blue fur. A single sweeping electric-blue speed trail curls behind his feet. At LEFT and RIGHT behind him, two small GTA supercars race but are clearly losing. The smooth road transitions naturally into chunky Minecraft grass and cobblestone near the lower frame, with distant sunny GTA towers. Very low dynamic camera, clean bright blue sky, motion blur only at edges; face and shoes tack-sharp. No printed finish banner, no extra creatures, no text or UI.

episodes.promise: The crew races through a shared adventure built from their favorite games; last place takes a pickle dunk.
how: Open overhead with Alex, Alan, Kat, Tanner and Shawn at their stations, then choose characters and vehicles.
Race from Rainbow Road through GTA City, the Nether and the End staging area into space; arrivals collect chests and keep moving.
Resolve the final space challenge, reveal the actual standings and deliver the pickle dunk.

intro.speaker: ALEX
intro.line: THIS is the world’s greatest video game.
intro.show: Start overhead with the crew standing at their PCs, then show one clear crossover moment.

intro.speaker: ALAN
intro.line: We put our favorite games into the same adventure. And last place takes a pickle dunk.
intro.show: Show the route and the real dunk payoff, then sit into the stations.

intro.speaker: CAST
intro.line: Can we choose a different punishment?
intro.show: Reveal the character/vehicle choices and begin the countdown.

turn: First one here gets the gold chest. Everyone else, choose carefully.
Let the first arrival open the gold chest while the others are still racing; reveal the next game-world surprise.
payoff: Last place has one final challenge—in real life.
Return from the space finale, reveal the actual standings, then show the pickle dunk and the crew’s reaction.
packaging: A superlative game promise × recognizable crossovers × a real-life consequence.
One impossible game collision and one strong twin reaction.
The first shot pays off the title; the route and punishment tell viewers why to stay.
episodes.support: The opening and route follow the October 23 production script. Public spectacle/race references support individual ingredients; there is no episode-specific CTR result.

refs.take: A recognizable game spectacle can be presented as one large visual idea.
A readable race objective supports the competitive opening.

artwork.title: I Found The Leaked GTA 6
artwork.alt: A photographic Stokes host is large at LEFT foreground holding one oversized transparent cyan USB drive close to camera, eyes wide in amazed disbelief. At RIGHT a single monitor shows a gorgeous sunny Miami-inspired GTA-style driving scene with a red supercar and palm boulevard, no HUD or branding. The translucent drive contains a tiny glowing city model as a visual metaphor. Bright gaming room with blue sky through a window. Face, drive and screen only; no labels, game packaging, company logo or leaked-source claim printed in the image.

artwork.title: I Found The Leaked GTA 6
artwork.alt: A photographic Stokes host fills RIGHT foreground playing with a controller, face delighted and amazed at a huge monitor at LEFT showing a bright Miami-style game city. Behind the monitor a second photographic identical-twin-style Stokes figure crouches in a plain red shirt with a mischievous grin and one finger to his lips, secretly holding a small remote trigger. Both faces use the supplied Stokes family likeness; foreground face dominant, prankster smaller. Sunny room, luminous blue sky through window. No words, no official logos, no threatening objects.

artwork.title: I Found The Leaked GTA 6
artwork.alt: A photographic Stokes host stands large at RIGHT foreground, astonished face toward camera, pulling back the corner of one giant glossy scenic wall like a stage curtain. The wall at LEFT depicts a bright realistic Miami-inspired game boulevard; behind the lifted corner we see an older, simpler GTA 5-style city set, a projector and one plain control console. A small red supercar is continuous across the front and revealed old set. One unified sunny soundstage-like game world with blue sky above, not a panel collage. The peeled edge is huge and instantly readable.

artwork.title: I Found The Leaked GTA 6
artwork.alt: A photographic Stokes host fills LEFT foreground pointing in shocked amusement toward one red supercar at RIGHT. The car is one continuous physical object: its front is incredibly glossy realistic metal and its rear visibly becomes a simpler old-game polygon wireframe with clean cyan edges. A small black projector on the ground illuminates the transformation boundary. Bright sunny Miami-style plaza, palm trees and blue sky. Close side-on view with clear front/rear change, only host and car dominate. No text, comparison panels, Nvidia logos or claim of a real leaked asset.

artwork.title: I Found The Leaked GTA 6
artwork.alt: A photographic Stokes host is large at CENTER foreground holding a controller with a baffled laughing expression. At LEFT foreground a tiny exquisite miniature Miami game city sits on a low table, with one small red model car. At RIGHT behind the miniature, a second Stokes twin-style figure in a red shirt operates a simple camera on a tripod aimed at the model and smiles mischievously. An oversized screen in far background shows only the camera view of the city, no HUD. Open sunny studio terrace with blue sky. Camera angle makes the tabletop illusion and prank operator obvious, not a random pile of gadgets.

episodes.promise: Convince Alex he is playing an early version of GTA 6, then escalate the absurdities until the reveal.
how: Present the setup as an apparent early-game opportunity and let Alex take the controller.
Begin with believable play, then introduce increasingly strange missions and characters.
Let the clues build to a clear reveal of how the prank was made.

intro.speaker: ALAN
intro.line: Alex thinks he’s about to play GTA 6. But we built this entire game to prank him.
intro.show: Show Alex arriving, then a quick behind-the-scenes glimpse for the audience.

intro.speaker: ALAN
intro.line: Every mission, every character, and every surprise is controlled by us.
intro.show: Tease two strange moments without revealing his biggest reaction.

intro.speaker: ALAN
intro.show: Let him sit down and begin the first believable mission.

turn: Let’s see how long it takes him to notice this.
Introduce the next clue after Alex has committed to the mission.
payoff: Alex, there’s something we need to tell you.
Reveal the prank, show how it was built and let Alex react.
packaging: An apparently impossible early-access opportunity × a twin prank.
Alex’s reaction to one unexpected GTA-style scene; the audience gets the prank context in the opening.
The title creates the opportunity; the first line makes the audience Alan’s accomplice.
episodes.support: Stokes prank history and controlled-game surprises support the structure. No actual Rockstar leak or endorsement is part of the pitch.

refs.take: A direct Stokes prank identity and escalating surprises.
A creator secretly changing the game supplies an adjacent prank mechanism.

artwork.title: I Survived 100 Hours in GTA
artwork.alt: A photographic Stokes host is large at RIGHT, leaning from an orange-red supercar racing diagonally toward the camera. At LEFT a blue supercar driven by one anonymous adult crew member draws level. Both cars pass under one simple black-and-white checkered finish arch on a sunny Miami-inspired coastal highway. One palm-lined skyline and turquoise ocean beyond. Low wide camera near the road, foreground host face sharp, only two cars and one finish. The game world is premium cinematic GTA-style rendering; the human is photographic.

artwork.title: I Survived 100 Hours in GTA
artwork.alt: A photographic Stokes host is CENTER foreground standing on the roof of one parked red supercar, waist-up and face large, raising a huge simple gold cup in both hands with triumphant excitement. Behind at RIGHT a small blue crew car is still racing toward a distant checkered arch. Sunlit Miami-style art-deco waterfront, turquoise water, palms and luminous blue sky. Eye-level hero portrait with trophy dominating upper LEFT, face center, car roof lower third. No prize money or game logo.

artwork.title: I Survived 100 Hours in GTA
artwork.alt: A photographic Stokes host fills LEFT foreground in the open driver seat of a red convertible, shocked face turned toward camera. At RIGHT the car is half on the edge of a broken coastal stunt-road segment, front tire just short of a safe landing ramp. A small blue crew car is already on the far side. Freeze the jump before any collision. Bright sunny Miami-inspired game world, water below and open blue sky. One red car, one gap and tiny blue rival; close dramatic perspective with a clear safe landing. No injury or explosion.

artwork.title: I Survived 100 Hours in GTA
artwork.alt: A real sunny studio with one large open window revealing a cinematic Miami game city outside. At LEFT foreground one photographic Stokes host in a black shirt holds a controller and looks toward camera in competitive excitement. At RIGHT two anonymous adult crew members in blue shirts share a second gaming station, one playing and one pointing toward the screen. One huge screen between the teams shows an orange car and blue car approaching a finish arch in the same scene, with no HUD. One unified physical room, not a split-panel collage. Strong blue sky through the window, faces large, simple color separation red/orange team versus blue crew.

artwork.title: I Survived 100 Hours in GTA
artwork.alt: A photographic Stokes host is CENTER foreground gripping the side rail of a red-and-black helicopter, face large in ecstatic urgency. The helicopter flies from lower RIGHT toward one rooftop helipad on a sunlit Miami-inspired tower at LEFT. A small blue crew helicopter approaches the same pad from the opposite direction, secondary. Turquoise bay and white high-rises far below, luminous blue sky filling upper half. Low camera outside the main cockpit, one host, one dominant helicopter and one clear final destination. No guns, HUD or text.

episodes.promise: The boys stay in one room until someone finishes GTA 6, while guests join for complete standalone challenges.
how: Start the room challenge and establish the agreed game finish point.
Follow the leading run, the setbacks and guest mission blocks while post receives finished segments.
When the first player finishes, release everyone and resolve the room story.

intro.speaker: ALEX
intro.line: We’re locked in this room until one of us beats GTA 6.
intro.show: Show the occupied stations, the room and the game starting.

intro.speaker: ALAN
intro.line: The first person to finish gets everyone out. And we’ve invited some help.
intro.show: Tease guest arrivals without claiming a booked guest who has not confirmed.

intro.speaker: ALEX
intro.line: Start the game. Let’s see who gets us out first.
intro.show: Begin the first mission and establish each player’s progress.

turn: We’ve been stuck here for hours. It’s time to call for help.
Bring in a confirmed guest with one specific mission to complete.
payoff: Show the actual final completion and the whole room’s release before the closing reaction.
packaging: A closed-room challenge × a long-awaited game × one clear release condition.
The twins in a visibly used gaming room, with one obvious exit and the game as context.
The unanswered question is who finishes first and how long the room story lasts.
episodes.support: Closed-goal survival and competitive gaming references support the ingredients. Guest appearances and the final recording duration remain unconfirmed.

refs.take: A single survival/completion goal carries a long progression.
Clear GTA objectives and player reactions keep the game story accessible.
